commits.message:
fix(color): a WINDOWS colour with no theme named is drawn in the console's own sixteen (rich-color-dhay)

Review of #266: at WINDOWS the writer picked slots by WINDOWS_TABLE but
getTruecolor and colorMath's drawnTable still fell back to the VGA sixteen,
so ensureContrast(#767676 on #0037da, 3) accepted a pair the console draws
at 1.81:1. resolveTerminal now takes the depth, and a WINDOWS colour with no
theme is drawn by the Windows console (Campbell); STANDARD and WINDOWS
convert to each other by keeping the slot, as Rich does, so a colour drawn
at WINDOWS reads as the console's colour whichever depth spelled it.

downgradeTable(depth) is the one table downgrade rounds against and the one
colorMath hands entries back from, replacing a second copy of that mapping.

Stale text: the colour-studio blurb called WINDOWS "not a downgrade target";
the README listed "standard"/"windows" colorSystem strings that throw.

Not taken: renaming a slot-kept colour to Rich's original name. Numbered
specs are compared by number (strip's vanishes reads name only when number
is absent) and the STANDARD downgrade already names by slot.

fix(color): ColorDepth.WINDOWS draws in the Windows console's sixteen colours (rich-color-dhay)

downgrade() ranked depths by enum value, and WINDOWS = 4 sits above
TRUECOLOR = 3, so nothing ever downgraded toward it and a WINDOWS console
wrote 24-bit SGR. Depths are now ranked by how many colours they name
(fidelity), and a downgrade to WINDOWS matches a fixed colour against
WINDOWS_TABLE while an ANSI slot keeps its index, as Rich does.

WINDOWS_TABLE was in console-attribute order (slot 1 navy) while every
reader of a WINDOWS number — its 30+n SGR, theme.ansiColors — takes it as
an ANSI index. It is now the Campbell scheme in ANSI order; the old values
reordered would have been STANDARD_TABLE exactly. colorMath's drawnTable
measures WINDOWS against that table instead of as truecolor.

fix(template-bindings): renderTemplate's error segment is one line fitted to maxWidth (rich-template-bindings-4bgw) (#265)

* fix(template-bindings): renderTemplate's error segment is one line fitted to maxWidth (rich-template-bindings-4bgw)

The caught error's message folds every line break to a space — an engine
message can carry one (`bad escape sequence \⏎`) — and the line is cut by
RichText.truncate at the same maxWidth the success path draws at, ending in
an ellipsis. The fixed 80-UTF-16-unit slice cut long messages mid-word and
dropped the fix hint (`wrap it: darken (color "primary") …`) with no mark.

The docs example now shows a long error fitted to the page's terminal.

* fix(template-bindings): error line folds every non-space whitespace; maxWidth is one value (rich-template-bindings-4bgw)

Review (high) on #265: a tab in the engine's message was counted as 0 cells
and drawn up to 8, so the fitted line could overflow maxWidth. The JSDoc and
docs now say the error line is fitted to maxWidth.
